question: Presbycusis (age-related sensorineural hearing loss) characteristically affects high-frequency sounds first, making it difficult for the elderly patient to understand speech in noisy environments.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is actually true. Presbycusis = high-frequency sensorineural loss. Consonants and speech in noisy environments (which require high-frequency discrimination) are most affected, while low-frequency awareness (vowels, bass sounds) is preserved longer.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Presbycusis begins with high-frequency hearing loss (loss of cochlear hair cells at the basal turn first). Consonants are high-frequency, so speech discrimination — particularly in noise — is impaired before pure tone thresholds.
